ui_bugs.issue: Locked stones do not navigate to /clarity-release when clicked. Spec: 'Clicking a locked Body Temple stone (e.g. stone-5 for non-premium) navigates to /clarity-release'. Actual: click is swallowed because line 391 reads `onClick={() => state !== 'locked' && handleStonePick(day)}` — when state==='locked' the handler is a no-op, so the parent's onStoneClick prop (which contains the navigate('/clarity-release') logic in BodyTemple.jsx lines 261-268) is never invoked. cursor is correctly 'not-allowed' and aria-label='Day N — locked', so the stones LOOK locked, but they are also UNRESPONSIVE which contradicts the upsell flow. Fix suggestion: allow the click through when an onStoneClick prop is provided by the consumer, e.g. `onClick={() => { if (onStoneClick) { onStoneClick(day); return; } if (state !== 'locked') handleStonePick(day); }}` — kids hubs (which rely on the internal popup) keep the current locked-is-noop behaviour because they do not pass onStoneClick, while Body Temple gets the navigation it needs.

action_items: Fix KidsJourneyPath.jsx line 391: allow click events to bubble to the parent-provided onStoneClick prop on locked stones (Body Temple needs to navigate locked premium stones to /clarity-release). Keep the existing locked-is-noop behaviour for kids hubs where no onStoneClick prop is passed, so the internal popup still ignores locked days.
critical_code_review_comments: KidsJourneyPath.jsx:391 — `onClick={() => state !== 'locked' && handleStonePick(day)}` overrides the contract advertised by the onStoneClick prop. The component should either always delegate to onStoneClick (and let the consumer decide what 'locked' means), or expose a `clickLocked` option. Currently the prop is silently dropped for locked stones, which is a leaky abstraction that already produced one shippable-blocker bug.

KidsJourneyPath.jsx — `cursor: 'not-allowed'` on locked stones is inconsistent with Body Temple's UX intent: in that screen, clicking a locked stone is a PREMIUM upsell trigger (route to /clarity-release), not a hard wall. Recommend cursor:'pointer' with a small lock badge so wanderers know it is a paywall, not a forbidden action.
KidsJourneyPath.jsx is 545 lines — close to the 700-line soft cap but acceptable. If the popup grows further, consider extracting <KidsJourneyPopup/> into its own file.

BodyTemple.jsx onStoneClick callback assumes overview.days_preview is fully populated (28 entries with is_premium). Verified in this iteration that the public endpoint returns all 28 with is_premium booleans, so the lookup is safe — but a fallback `if (!d) navigate('/clarity-release');` would protect against future API trimming.

Kids hubs / Daily / Activities each fetch /api/kids-journey/progress independently on mount — three round-trips per session on a slow network. Caching the response in a lightweight context (or relying on the existing react-query if available) would shave ~600ms off the second-page render.

All three kids age-themed paths (pebbles=little-dreamers, crystals=explorers, hexagons=dreamweavers) render correctly with the right testids; their internal popup (kids-journey-popup + -message + -daily + -activities + -close) works on kids hubs because no onStoneClick prop is passed. Also re-confirm that on kids hubs the locked-stone behaviour is UNCHANGED (clicking a locked stone on /kids-universe/explorers/hub should still open the internal popup — NOT navigate anywhere). The backend pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_kids_journey.py is green and can be run with `KIDS_JOURNEY_TEST_BACKEND=<public-url> pytest backend/tests/test_kids_journey.py -v`.
rca of the issue: Root cause: KidsJourneyPath.jsx line 391 hard-codes `state !== 'locked'` as a gate before invoking handleStonePick. handleStonePick is the function that ultimately calls the parent's onStoneClick prop (Body Temple's navigate-to-clarity-release logic). So locked stones in Body Temple never get a chance to redirect users to the premium funnel. Reproduction: open /body-temple as anonymous → click any stone with day>=2 → URL stays on /body-temple (expected: /clarity-release). Mitigation: change line 391 to honour onStoneClick for locked stones when the prop is provided; preserve current behaviour when prop is absent (kids hubs). One-line fix described in action_items.
